whatChanged.title: Complete written responses became a clearer priority
whatChanged.summary: A partir das aulas de Geography em agosto, ficou mais claro que o próximo passo é transformar o que Eduarda entende em respostas completas em inglês, especialmente ao explicar conteúdos da escola com as próprias palavras.
whatChanged.evidence: The 17 August lesson identified written Geography responses as a difficulty, and the 19–20 August lessons continued to require guided production.

priorities.title: Transformar ideias em respostas completas
priorities.why: Continuar construindo respostas claras em inglês, começando pela própria tentativa e usando apoio quando ele realmente ajudar.

priorities.title: Usar can e should para comunicar ideias
priorities.why: Levar can/can't e should/shouldn't dos exercícios guiados para situações em que Eduarda escolhe a forma que melhor expressa o que quer dizer.

priorities.title: Explicar Geography em inglês
priorities.why: Conectar o conhecimento de Geography à capacidade de explicar economic sectors, water cycle e outros conteúdos em frases próprias.

nextAction.outcome: Observe what Eduarda can answer independently before adding models or prompts.
nextAction.title: Next challenge: six quick questions
nextAction.description: Na próxima aula, Eduarda começa com seis perguntas curtas sobre abilities, advice e Geography. Primeiro ela tenta do seu jeito; depois o professor acrescenta pistas quando forem úteis. Assim, a próxima aula pode partir exatamente do ponto em que ela está.
nextAction.evidence: Recent lessons show that complete responses, modal choice and Geography explanations still need to be checked with less support.

schedule.label: Support lessons are booked when needed. No future lesson is currently confirmed.

progressTracker.title: Putting ideas into full answers / Transformar ideias em respostas
progressTracker.insight: Eduarda já vem trabalhando respostas sobre conteúdos da escola. O próximo passo é organizar essas ideias em frases cada vez mais completas com menos ajuda.

progressTracker.title: Can & should in context / Usar can e should com sentido
progressTracker.insight: Can/can't e should/shouldn't já apareceram em atividades de ability, permission e advice. Agora vamos criar novas oportunidades para Eduarda escolher e usar essas formas em suas próprias respostas.

progressTracker.title: Geography through English / Geografia em inglês
progressTracker.insight: Economic sectors e water cycle já fizeram parte da jornada. O próximo ciclo vai ajudar Eduarda a transformar esse conhecimento em explicações simples e claras em inglês.

progressTracker.title: Know it & explain it / Saber e explicar
progressTracker.insight: Uma força importante desta jornada é trabalhar duas coisas juntas: compreender o conteúdo da escola e encontrar o inglês necessário para explicá-lo.

progressTracker.title: Try first, then build / Tentar e depois construir
progressTracker.insight: Nas próximas atividades, Eduarda terá espaço para tentar primeiro. As pistas entram depois, ajudando a transformar cada tentativa em uma resposta mais completa.

classReports.title: Class Report — 02 Jul 2026
classReports.summary: Practice of Present Simple, do/does, frequency and should/shouldn't focused on routines, questions and advice.
classReports.teacherInsight: Transfer points — Evidence: guided practice of routines, questions, frequency and advice. Boundary: independent mastery was not measured. Next verification: produce complete routine and advice responses before a model is provided.

classReports.title: Class Report — 06 Jul 2026
classReports.summary: Geography work covered rural areas, primary, secondary and tertiary sectors, tourism and production chains in English.
classReports.teacherInsight: Transfer points — Evidence: economic sectors and production-chain concepts were connected to English vocabulary. Boundary: retention was not independently assessed. Next verification: classify and explain a sector or activity in Eduarda's own English sentence.

classReports.title: Class Report — 08 Jul 2026
classReports.summary: Economic activities and environmental themes were revisited, reinforcing links between school content and English vocabulary.
classReports.teacherInsight: Transfer points — Evidence: prior Geography content was revisited in English. Boundary: continuity of content is not measured progress. Next verification: explain one economic-activity or environment relationship in her own words.

classReports.title: Class Report — 17 Aug 2026
classReports.summary: Eduarda reported that Geography was harder when written responses were required. The lesson reviewed economic sectors and made complete written answers a clearer priority.
classReports.teacherInsight: Transfer points — Evidence: reported difficulty with written answers now informs the complete-response priority. Interpretation: Geography must be checked in two layers — concept and English formulation. Next verification: explain primary sector, industry and fish in her own sentences; no school grade is reconstructed.

classReports.title: Class Report — 18 Aug 2026
classReports.summary: A guided Geography review focused on the water cycle and related urban-environment concepts, with reading, repetition and supported retrieval.
classReports.teacherInsight: Transfer points — Evidence: water-cycle vocabulary was retrieved with support. Boundary: term recognition does not establish independent conceptual explanation. Next verification: explain evaporation, precipitation and runoff in simple sentences with reduced support.

classReports.title: Class Report — 19 Aug 2026
classReports.summary: Review of can/can't for ability and permission, should/shouldn't for advice and adverbs of frequency included short guided oral production.
classReports.teacherInsight: Transfer points — Evidence: Eduarda produced a relevant sentence in guided practice and answered with modals. Boundary: frequent prompts and models mean independent selection is not yet established. Next verification: distinguish ability or permission from advice in complete student-authored sentences.

classReports.title: Class Report — 20 Aug 2026
classReports.summary: Final English exam review combined can/can't, should/shouldn't, adverbs of frequency, sentence organization and reading comprehension with teacher support.
classReports.teacherInsight: Transfer points — Evidence: the lesson shows continuity from 19 August across reading, modals and sentence work. Boundary: supported recovery of can or should and reading comprehension do not prove independent production. Next verification: answer short questions first without a model, then compare with a supported version.

grammarOverview.title: Grammar & Accuracy Overview
grammarOverview.summary: Keep grammar connected to the school tasks you are working on, with increasing independence.
focusPoints: Present Simple: practiced in July for statements, negatives, questions and frequency; current independent control still needs checking.
Can / can't: practiced in August for ability and permission; verify student-authored sentences with the base verb.
Should / shouldn't: practiced in July and August for advice; verify modal choice and base-verb construction without a model.

teacherFeedback.title: General Feedback
teacherFeedback.body: Eduarda participates in school-support tasks and produces responses in guided practice. The follow-up considers not only the final answer but also the amount of support needed to reach it.

teacherFeedback.title: Growth Priority
teacherFeedback.body: Increase complete student-authored responses and gradually reduce the need for teacher support.

cumulativeImpact.title: Longitudinal School-Support Record

The teacher-corrected portfolio records CEFR A1 as current level and CEFR A2 as target; the lesson history does not by itself establish advancement to A2 or independent mastery.
